correctness.rationale: The common factor 1/s changing discounted transforms to the specified s^(n-1) cycle weights cancels in Q=F_0/(F_0+F_a). Tridiagonal cofactors give odds C s^(2z-a) D_right/D_left: the product of steps to each endpoint pairs with the continuant on the opposite side. Every restricted transient transition matrix has spectral radius below one (uniformly positive chance of exiting its finite interval in bounded time); it is similar to a symmetric bipartite matrix. Thus continuants are positive products of 1-lambda²s² on [0,1], and nonincreasing. Reflect to z<=a/2; off-center for a<=6 this gives z<=2, D_left=1, and a strictly decreasing power factor. At the midpoint only constant odds (a=2,4) or a ratio of two linear factors in s² (a=6) occur. At a=7 the only new sites are 3 and 4. At z=3 the derivative sign is N(t)=-1+(3b-A)t-Abt², t=s². It is negative if b<=A, since N(t)=-(1-bt)²+(b-A)t(1+bt); otherwise N'(t)>0 on [0,1]. The unique interior minimum occurs precisely when N(1)>0; equality is only an endpoint stationary point. The smaller quadratic root gives the stated s_*. Reflection exchanges exit sides and gives a maximum, not a second minimum. Substitution of the exact witness gives b=16/25, A=1/2, C=32/25, Q(1)=16/25 and the claimed radical. Its reevaluated numerical values are s_*=0.9369685842877506 and Q(s_*)=0.6362752323028685.
residual_risks: The recorded finite checks are supplementary; universal exclusion is proved by the continuant argument. The conclusion is for the indicated exit-side convention, not absorption time or arbitrary reset clocks.

evidence: Newton and Vega Coso explicitly leave classification of interior reset extrema open in section 10.3. Vega Coso's midpoint theorem assumes homogeneous jump probabilities. The larger-size threshold excludes two extrema, not one.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general formula and sufficient monotonicity tests are useful ingredients but do not supply the stated inhomogeneous finite-size exclusion and sharp iff criterion. Homogeneity does not imply the arbitrary-environment conclusion.

evidence: Weighted renewal and the single-target Gillis walk address different conclusions. The two-extrema theorem gives a bound on pairwise multiplicity, compatible with a lower threshold for one.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even a proven twelve-state minimum for two cannot exclude one at seven states or furnish the necessary and sufficient inequality for the eight-state response. The frozen result uses standard continuants for a different sharp classification.

value.rationale: This resolves a minimal nonmonotonicity question for the natural endpoint observable under geometric restarting, within the broader open classification for arbitrary birth–death environments. It gives both universal exclusion below the threshold and the exact phase boundary for all environments at the first size; the rational witness is not an isolated numerical optimization.
residual_risks: No general classification for larger paths or non-geometric clocks is implied.
